# What belongs in a source-code delivery?

Start with an inventory rather than an assumption. A source-code archive, a runnable project, a complete backend, and an App Store listing are different deliverables.

## Ask for a concrete file list

Record whether the package includes the Xcode project or workspace, source files, local data models, assets, dependency manifests, setup documentation, and sample data. If a backend is involved, ask which server components are included and which must be operated separately.

## Separate access from ownership

An app listing or a seller's demo account can help you evaluate behavior. Neither establishes that those accounts or distribution rights are part of a source-code purchase. Record the actual deliverables and read the applicable terms.

## Check setup prerequisites

List any credentials, domains, service plans, devices, or paid tools required to reproduce the demo. If a configuration file is intentionally excluded because it contains secrets, request a redacted example and field descriptions.

## Preserve evidence

Keep the delivery inventory, package version, and original archive together. When an item is missing, describe the expected file or behavior precisely so support can reproduce the problem.
